candidates.rationale: Rising leverage over the past quarter combined with currently elevated income-inflating accruals compounds balance-sheet and earnings-quality risk at once; gating on an elevated dollar-volume percentile targets names where this deterioration is fresh news still being priced in rather than already stale.

High operating margin marks a firm with a resilient, well-understood cash-flow story, so when its very-short-term return volatility spikes above its own three-week baseline the move is more likely a transient liquidity shock than a fundamental re-rating, and should revert faster than the same vol spike in a low-margin name.

A rising accrual component (earnings propped up by non-cash items) arriving alongside a simultaneously deteriorating operating margin is a compounding earnings-quality red flag: the reported number is being flattered exactly when the underlying operating business is genuinely eroding.

Earnings generated alongside high asset turnover reflect profitability earned through efficient asset use rather than pricing power or leverage; ranking that jointly-efficient earnings measure against current accrual risk isolates operationally-backed earnings from those merely inflated by aggressive accounting.

Earnings power scaled by financial leverage is a risk-adjusted quality cushion, so an unusually large single-day price move is more likely a transient overreaction that reverts when a firm has ample earnings per unit of balance-sheet risk, versus the same move in a levered, weak earner where it may reflect real solvency news.

Stocks ranking high on both an asset-efficiency measure and an absolute earnings-power measure at once signal broader-based quality than either ratio alone; spreading that joint score against how erratic (not how large) the stock's own recent volume has been isolates quality names in an unstable liquidity regime where mispricing is harder to arbitrage away.

A quarter-over-quarter rise in accruals is a fresh earnings-quality deterioration signal that the market digests gradually; ranking that change against the stock's own very-recent relative trading-activity percentile separates newly-deteriorating names not yet drawing attention from those the market has already started trading on.

Return-volume co-movement over the past month proxies for how information-driven recent trading has been; conditioning that co-movement on strong per-share earnings identifies profitable firms undergoing genuinely informed accumulation, versus the same correlation pattern in a weak earner that is more likely speculative churn.

The number of days in the past month a stock traded above its own quarterly-average volume measures the breadth and persistence of elevated attention rather than a single spike; ranking that attention-breadth measure against leverage tests whether sustained above-average trading in highly-levered names reflects the market progressively working through financial-risk concerns.

Operating margin (pricing power and cost control) and return-on-assets (efficiency of the full asset base) capture distinct dimensions of quality; a firm ranking far higher on one than the other has a profitability mix the market is less likely to price carefully than either single ratio.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Dividing a fundamental delta by a raw price level ($close) before ranking erased the signal (|t| 0.10). Cross-sectional variance in price level dominates the ratio and swamps the fundamental term.
  2. Flipping only the top-level +/- combinator while leaving both child subtrees untouched still reads as the same archive member (10 shared nodes). A combinator swap needs a change inside at least one child to count as a new fusion.
  3. RANK(fundamental level) - RANK($dollar_volume) was this round's strongest and simplest kernel (fitness 6.115, medium/mixed niche). earnings_per_share now joins accrual_gap/roa as a fundamental that pairs well against a raw dollar_volume level in a plain rank spread.
  4. $accrual_gap paired additively with a second fundamental's TS-derived leg accepted twice this round at strong fitness (leverage-volatility 3.558, book_per_share-delta 5.152), a reliable anchor for slow/fundamental rank-spread proposals.
  5. TS_RANK($high - $low, w) crossed with any CS_RANK(...) term (product, or nested in a spread) is exhausted: 6 of 20 rejects this round were archive_subtree hits on this leaf against 3 different archived parents, regardless of window (10/21/42) or the CS_RANK partner's field. Stop proposing this shape.
  6. Combine two fundamentals first (product, or a guarded ratio), then spread with RANK(...)-RANK(...) against a third distinct fundamental — this took 3 of the round's 4 best accepts (3.579, 3.227, 3.144). Bare fundamental-minus-fundamental still fails; roa/leverage/operating_margin and accrual_gap/book_per_share/roe are now taken triples, so pick a fresh combination of three.
  7. All 10 accepts this round landed in a '.../low' turnover niche; none reached medium/high or mixed/high. Target those niches explicitly next round instead of adding more low-turnover fundamental spreads.
  8. RANK(a) + RANK(b) addition underperforms the RANK(a) - RANK(b) spread: this round's one addition-combinator proposal failed cheap_screen (|t| 0.32) while 8 of 10 accepts were subtraction spreads. Default to the spread form for two-rank composites.
  9. Short-window raw price differences are return-equivalent for cheap_screen, not just price ratios: TS_DELTA($close, 3) failed twice under different partners this round (|t| 0.47, 0.55). Avoid <=5-day TS_DELTA on a bare OHLC field as a standalone leg.
  10. DELAY's lag argument decorrelates like a TS_MEAN window: wrapping a previously-bare leaf in DELAY(field, 1), or re-lagging an existing DELAY, failed the correlation gate twice this round (rho 0.976, 0.819). Edit a structural node instead of a DELAY lag alone.
  11. TS_MIN($low, w) at a small window is a near-substitute for bare $low inside an extremum ratio — swapping one for the other, or just re-windowing the TS_MIN, didn't decorrelate (rho 0.954, 0.871). Vary the ratio's structure, not which extremum window feeds it.
  12. TS_CORR(ABS($return), TS_RANK($volume, w), 63) accepted at 3.420, so the ABS(return)/TS_RANK(volume) fix holds beyond the previously-validated 21-day correlation window — keep varying this window rather than treating the pairing as used up.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
